**Smash Mouth** is an American rock band from San Jose, California.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-3) The band was formed in 1994[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-4) and was originally composed of Steve Harwell (lead vocals), Kevin Coleman (drums), Greg Camp (guitar), and Paul De Lisle (bass). Harwell's departure in 2021 left De Lisle as the sole remaining original member. They are known for their songs "[Walkin' on the Sun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walkin'_on_the_Sun "Walkin' on the Sun")" (1997), "All Star" (1999),[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-5) and "Then the Morning Comes" (1999), as well as [a cover](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I'm_a_Believer_(Smash_Mouth_song) "I'm a Believer (Smash Mouth song)") of The Monkees' "[I'm a Believer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I'm_a_Believer "I'm a Believer")" (2001).

The band adopted retro styles covering several decades of popular music. They have also performed numerous covers of popular songs, including War's "[Why Can't We Be Friends?](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Why_Can't_We_Be_Friends%3F_(song) "Why Can't We Be Friends? (song)")", Rick Astley's "Never Gonna Give You Up", Simple Minds' "[Don't You (Forget About Me)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don't_You_(Forget_About_Me) "Don't You (Forget About Me)")", ? & the Mysterians' "[Can't Get Enough of You Baby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Can't_Get_Enough_of_You_Baby "Can't Get Enough of You Baby")", the Beatles' "Getting Better", Queen's "Under Pressure", House of Pain's "Jump Around", and "[I Wan'na Be Like You](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Wan'na_Be_Like_You "I Wan'na Be Like You")" from _The Jungle Book_. They also composed two songs for the South Korean animated film _Pororo, The Racing Adventure_: "Beside Myself" and "Everything Just Crazy".
The group's debut album _Fush Yu Mang_ has been certified platinum twice by the RIAA and their second album _Astro Lounge_ has since been certified platinum thrice. Their song "All Star" was nominated for a Grammy Award for Best Pop Performance by a Duo or Group with Vocals in 2001.
Smash Mouth's roots trace back to 1990 when Steve Harwell and Kevin Coleman met. Smash Mouth was then formed in 1994 by Harwell, who had formerly played in a rap group called F.O.S. (Freedom of Speech). Coleman, who was Harwell's manager, knew guitarist Greg Camp and bassist Paul De Lisle, who had both played in a local punk band, and introduced the three musicians to each other. They began rehearsing together along with Coleman, who played drums. They soon developed into a band, and named themselves Smashmouth, an American football term. During their early years, the band played largely rock music.

The band's first publicity came when a demo of the song "Nervous in the Alley" was played by a San Jose radio station, KOME. Soon after, Interscope Records signed the band, and the group's debut album, _Fush Yu Mang_, was released in 1997, featuring another member: the keyboardist Michael Klooster. Also, upon signing to Interscope Records, the band changed their name from Smashmouth to Smash Mouth. The album saw commercial success peaking at number 19 on the US Billboard 200 and number 23 in Canada.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-:0-6) It was led by the band's first major single "[Walkin' on the Sun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walkin'_on_the_Sun "Walkin' on the Sun")" which peaked at number 1 on the US Adult Top 40 and Alternative Songs charts and at number 3 in Canada.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-:0-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-7) The singles "The Fonz" and a cover of "[Why Can't We Be Friends](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Why_Can't_We_Be_Friends_(song) "Why Can't We Be Friends (song)")" from the 1998 Kevin Bacon film _Wild Things_ were also subsequently released. The album has since gone double platinum. During this time the band officially started touring regularly even opening for U2 on their PopMart Tour and got their first television appearance as the musical guest on episode 157 of _Oddville, MTV._[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-8)

### 1998–2004: rise to fame, _Astro Lounge_, _Smash Mouth_, and _Get the Picture?_
[edit | edit source]
The band's second album, _Astro Lounge_, was released in 1999 and marked a change in direction, as it had less of the previous ska influence and more of a pop sound. It led to more publicity for the band, and ended up being one of the most critically acclaimed albums from the group. It peaked at number 6 on the US Billboard 200, the highest the band has ever charted in the states, and reached the top 20 in both Canada and New Zealand.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-9) Supported by the hit single "All Star" (which was featured in several film soundtracks, most notably in _Shrek_ (2001), although the official music video references _Mystery Men_) the song reached number 4 on both the Billboard hot 100 and Australia it then charted even higher in Canada peaking at number 2.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-:0-6)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-10) "Then the Morning Comes" was also a hit for the band and peaked a number 11 on the Billboard hot 100.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-:0-6)_Astro Lounge_ has since been certified as triple platinum.

### Hey Now: a story of alt-rock, soundtracks and fleeting fame
Article and interview Pete Crigler
(December 2023)
Smash Mouth were one of the more popular alt-rock groups of the late '90's, scoring hits with "Walkin' on the Sun" and the ubiquitous "All Star." By the early 2000's, they had pivoted into a more commercial pop direction and after 2001, they dropped off the charts in a supremely quick fashion. Their music always lingered and so did the band, down to two original members, playing state fairs, food and wine festivals and donating songs to Dr. Seuss movies and Hot Wheels video games. In 2021, singer Steve Harwell left the band after a disastrous show, citing mental health and physical maladies including heart issues. In September of 2023, he passed away at the age of 56 because of liver failure. I decided to write about the band's legacy and some of the ways they still resonate even with a lot of crap material in their catalogue.  
The band formed in the mid-'90s after Harwell failed at a rap career, starting a group called F.O.S. and signing a deal with Scotti Bros, home of Weird Al Yankovic. After one failed single, Harwell decided to change tactic. He teamed up with his friend, amateur drummer Kevin Coleman and began devising a new project. By 1995, they had teamed up with guitarist/songwriter Greg Camp and bassist Paul DeLisle and started Smash Mouth. In 1996, the band signed with Interscope and went into the studio with producer Eric Valentine, who was simultaneously working on the debut album by Third Eye Blind. In the summer of 1997, Smash Mouth released _Fush Yu Mang_, a garbled statement made by Al Pacino in _Scarface_. The album's first single was about to change the band's lives forever.

### Hey Now: a story of alt-rock, soundtracks and fleeting fame
That song, a perfect piece of alt-pop written by Greg Camp, "Walkin' on the Sun" was damn near perfect for the summer of 1997 and went to number one on the alternative charts and was all over MTV. It's a song that I still cherish today and think is one of the best alt rock songs of the late '90's. Hooky, very poppy and retro as all hell, the song takes you back to a moment in time and never lets up. One of those songs that to me just feels timeless and sounds good no matter when you're listening to it.
The album is a fun little blast of alt rock with touches of sixties pop and ska amongst others. Good tracks like "Flo," "Disconnect the Dots" and "Let's Rock" are just fun alt rock without too much thought. The album's other main single was a cover of War's "Why Can't We Be Friends" which was featured in _BASEketball_ but hasn't really held up as well. The album eventually went double platinum and the band spent the next year and a half touring and contributing to soundtracks. The most notable was a cover of ? and the Mysterians' "Can't Get Enough of You (Baby)" from the _Can't Hardly Wait_ soundtrack which became the band's next big hit. My personal favorite is a Camp sung track entitled "Sorry About Your Penis," a humorous track found on the soundtrack of the Trey Parker movie _Orgazmo_. Definitely a track worth tracking down for its sheer lunacy and catchiness.

### Hey Now: a story of alt-rock, soundtracks and fleeting fame
Then the band went back to work on their sophomore record. At first in the early part of 1999, Interscope told them they didn't have a single. This led Camp to come up with "Then the Morning Comes." By spring, the album was ready and the label decided to go with "All Star," having decided after all that the album had enough singles. The album, entitled, _Astro Lounge_ was launched in summer of '99 with "All Star." The video was tied to the Ben Stiller superhero comedy _Mystery Men_ and it was quickly all over MTV. The song went to number two on the modern rock chart and crossed over big time to the Billboard Hot 100 where it peaked at number four. The song was one of the most ubiquitous of the year and is still thought of fondly by those of us coming of age around that time.
Drummer Kevin Coleman left during this time and was at first replaced by Tripping Daisy/Brave Combo drummer Mitch Marine before being permanently replaced in 2000 by Cracker/Spent Poets drummer Michael Urbano. "Then the Morning Comes" was released as the second single in late '99 and peaked at number 11 on the hot 100. Around this time, the band began shifting their sound to a more pop oriented flavor, losing a lot of the alternative and ska elements that had helped them initially. The album's third single, a ballad called "Waste," was released in spring of 2000. I had loved the song when it came out but looking back, I must not have remembered it too well for it wasn't as interesting, a little too poppy for my taste. "Then the Morning Comes" has become one of my favorite songs by the band because of the infectiousness and AM-pop leanings of the track. Just a song that deserves to be remembered more.

### Hey Now: a story of alt-rock, soundtracks and fleeting fame
During this time, the band's soundtrack appearances began shifting from the alternative like "Half-Baked" to the more commercial. Though they did contribute a cover of Let's Active's "Every Word Means No" to a _Friends_ comp and a great version of Steely Dan's "Do It Again" to the Jim Carrey comedy _Me, Myself & Irene_, they also appeared with the album track "Come on Come On" for the Nickelodeon kids flick _Snow Day_ and "All Star" was heard in the "Digimon" animated movie, one of many times that song would be used in film. Let's not forget "Better Do It Right" for the Jim Carrey _How the Grinch Stole Christmas_ movie. After touring wrapped sometime in 2000, the band took a break before beginning the next album.
In the spring of 2001, DreamWorks Animation announced their big new film, _Shrek_, which was based on the books by William Steig. The filmmakers needed a song to help introduce the character. The story goes they'd been using "All Star" as a temp track to be replaced by something else but they couldn't find anything else that worked so the song became the lead-in for the whole movie. In addition, the band agreed to record a cover of the Monkees' chestnut "I'm a Believer" for the end credits.
As everyone knows, the film became a blockbuster, one of the biggest hits of the year and one of the most well-regarded animated movies of the early 2000's. "I'm a Believer" became a hit all over again and peaked at number 25 on the hot 100. The movie sealed the reputation of "All Star" as pop culture canon for years to come and even though I couldn't tolerate "I'm a Believer," I couldn't help but think about how amazing it was that the band still had a career as rock groups like them were starting to become a thing of the past. It's here where the story gets a little darker and perhaps foreshadows the end.

### Hey Now: a story of alt-rock, soundtracks and fleeting fame
Article and interview Pete Crigler
(December 2023)
Smash Mouth were one of the more popular alt-rock groups of the late '90's, scoring hits with "Walkin' on the Sun" and the ubiquitous "All Star." By the early 2000's, they had pivoted into a more commercial pop direction and after 2001, they dropped off the charts in a supremely quick fashion. Their music always lingered and so did the band, down to two original members, playing state fairs, food and wine festivals and donating songs to Dr. Seuss movies and Hot Wheels video games. In 2021, singer Steve Harwell left the band after a disastrous show, citing mental health and physical maladies including heart issues. In September of 2023, he passed away at the age of 56 because of liver failure. I decided to write about the band's legacy and some of the ways they still resonate even with a lot of crap material in their catalogue.  
The band formed in the mid-'90s after Harwell failed at a rap career, starting a group called F.O.S. and signing a deal with Scotti Bros, home of Weird Al Yankovic. After one failed single, Harwell decided to change tactic. He teamed up with his friend, amateur drummer Kevin Coleman and began devising a new project. By 1995, they had teamed up with guitarist/songwriter Greg Camp and bassist Paul DeLisle and started Smash Mouth. In 1996, the band signed with Interscope and went into the studio with producer Eric Valentine, who was simultaneously working on the debut album by Third Eye Blind. In the summer of 1997, Smash Mouth released _Fush Yu Mang_, a garbled statement made by Al Pacino in _Scarface_. The album's first single was about to change the band's lives forever.
texts.2:
### Hey Now: a story of alt-rock, soundtracks and fleeting fame
That song, a perfect piece of alt-pop written by Greg Camp, "Walkin' on the Sun" was damn near perfect for the summer of 1997 and went to number one on the alternative charts and was all over MTV. It's a song that I still cherish today and think is one of the best alt rock songs of the late '90's. Hooky, very poppy and retro as all hell, the song takes you back to a moment in time and never lets up. One of those songs that to me just feels timeless and sounds good no matter when you're listening to it.
The album is a fun little blast of alt rock with touches of sixties pop and ska amongst others. Good tracks like "Flo," "Disconnect the Dots" and "Let's Rock" are just fun alt rock without too much thought. The album's other main single was a cover of War's "Why Can't We Be Friends" which was featured in _BASEketball_ but hasn't really held up as well. The album eventually went double platinum and the band spent the next year and a half touring and contributing to soundtracks. The most notable was a cover of ? and the Mysterians' "Can't Get Enough of You (Baby)" from the _Can't Hardly Wait_ soundtrack which became the band's next big hit. My personal favorite is a Camp sung track entitled "Sorry About Your Penis," a humorous track found on the soundtrack of the Trey Parker movie _Orgazmo_. Definitely a track worth tracking down for its sheer lunacy and catchiness.
texts.3:
### Hey Now: a story of alt-rock, soundtracks and fleeting fame
Then the band went back to work on their sophomore record. At first in the early part of 1999, Interscope told them they didn't have a single. This led Camp to come up with "Then the Morning Comes." By spring, the album was ready and the label decided to go with "All Star," having decided after all that the album had enough singles. The album, entitled, _Astro Lounge_ was launched in summer of '99 with "All Star." The video was tied to the Ben Stiller superhero comedy _Mystery Men_ and it was quickly all over MTV. The song went to number two on the modern rock chart and crossed over big time to the Billboard Hot 100 where it peaked at number four. The song was one of the most ubiquitous of the year and is still thought of fondly by those of us coming of age around that time.
Drummer Kevin Coleman left during this time and was at first replaced by Tripping Daisy/Brave Combo drummer Mitch Marine before being permanently replaced in 2000 by Cracker/Spent Poets drummer Michael Urbano. "Then the Morning Comes" was released as the second single in late '99 and peaked at number 11 on the hot 100. Around this time, the band began shifting their sound to a more pop oriented flavor, losing a lot of the alternative and ska elements that had helped them initially. The album's third single, a ballad called "Waste," was released in spring of 2000. I had loved the song when it came out but looking back, I must not have remembered it too well for it wasn't as interesting, a little too poppy for my taste. "Then the Morning Comes" has become one of my favorite songs by the band because of the infectiousness and AM-pop leanings of the track. Just a song that deserves to be remembered more.
texts.4:
### Hey Now: a story of alt-rock, soundtracks and fleeting fame
During this time, the band's soundtrack appearances began shifting from the alternative like "Half-Baked" to the more commercial. Though they did contribute a cover of Let's Active's "Every Word Means No" to a _Friends_ comp and a great version of Steely Dan's "Do It Again" to the Jim Carrey comedy _Me, Myself & Irene_, they also appeared with the album track "Come on Come On" for the Nickelodeon kids flick _Snow Day_ and "All Star" was heard in the "Digimon" animated movie, one of many times that song would be used in film. Let's not forget "Better Do It Right" for the Jim Carrey _How the Grinch Stole Christmas_ movie. After touring wrapped sometime in 2000, the band took a break before beginning the next album.
In the spring of 2001, DreamWorks Animation announced their big new film, _Shrek_, which was based on the books by William Steig. The filmmakers needed a song to help introduce the character. The story goes they'd been using "All Star" as a temp track to be replaced by something else but they couldn't find anything else that worked so the song became the lead-in for the whole movie. In addition, the band agreed to record a cover of the Monkees' chestnut "I'm a Believer" for the end credits.
As everyone knows, the film became a blockbuster, one of the biggest hits of the year and one of the most well-regarded animated movies of the early 2000's. "I'm a Believer" became a hit all over again and peaked at number 25 on the hot 100. The movie sealed the reputation of "All Star" as pop culture canon for years to come and even though I couldn't tolerate "I'm a Believer," I couldn't help but think about how amazing it was that the band still had a career as rock groups like them were starting to become a thing of the past. It's here where the story gets a little darker and perhaps foreshadows the end.

texts.1: **Smash Mouth** is an American rock band from San Jose, California.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-3) The band was formed in 1994[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-4) and was originally composed of Steve Harwell (lead vocals), Kevin Coleman (drums), Greg Camp (guitar), and Paul De Lisle (bass). Harwell's departure in 2021 left De Lisle as the sole remaining original member. They are known for their songs "[Walkin' on the Sun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walkin'_on_the_Sun "Walkin' on the Sun")" (1997), "All Star" (1999),[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-5) and "Then the Morning Comes" (1999), as well as [a cover](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I'm_a_Believer_(Smash_Mouth_song) "I'm a Believer (Smash Mouth song)") of The Monkees' "[I'm a Believer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I'm_a_Believer "I'm a Believer")" (2001).
texts.2:
The band adopted retro styles covering several decades of popular music. They have also performed numerous covers of popular songs, including War's "[Why Can't We Be Friends?](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Why_Can't_We_Be_Friends%3F_(song) "Why Can't We Be Friends? (song)")", Rick Astley's "Never Gonna Give You Up", Simple Minds' "[Don't You (Forget About Me)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don't_You_(Forget_About_Me) "Don't You (Forget About Me)")", ? & the Mysterians' "[Can't Get Enough of You Baby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Can't_Get_Enough_of_You_Baby "Can't Get Enough of You Baby")", the Beatles' "Getting Better", Queen's "Under Pressure", House of Pain's "Jump Around", and "[I Wan'na Be Like You](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Wan'na_Be_Like_You "I Wan'na Be Like You")" from _The Jungle Book_. They also composed two songs for the South Korean animated film _Pororo, The Racing Adventure_: "Beside Myself" and "Everything Just Crazy".
The group's debut album _Fush Yu Mang_ has been certified platinum twice by the RIAA and their second album _Astro Lounge_ has since been certified platinum thrice. Their song "All Star" was nominated for a Grammy Award for Best Pop Performance by a Duo or Group with Vocals in 2001.
Smash Mouth's roots trace back to 1990 when Steve Harwell and Kevin Coleman met. Smash Mouth was then formed in 1994 by Harwell, who had formerly played in a rap group called F.O.S. (Freedom of Speech). Coleman, who was Harwell's manager, knew guitarist Greg Camp and bassist Paul De Lisle, who had both played in a local punk band, and introduced the three musicians to each other. They began rehearsing together along with Coleman, who played drums. They soon developed into a band, and named themselves Smashmouth, an American football term. During their early years, the band played largely rock music.
texts.3: The band's first publicity came when a demo of the song "Nervous in the Alley" was played by a San Jose radio station, KOME. Soon after, Interscope Records signed the band, and the group's debut album, _Fush Yu Mang_, was released in 1997, featuring another member: the keyboardist Michael Klooster. Also, upon signing to Interscope Records, the band changed their name from Smashmouth to Smash Mouth. The album saw commercial success peaking at number 19 on the US Billboard 200 and number 23 in Canada.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-:0-6) It was led by the band's first major single "[Walkin' on the Sun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walkin'_on_the_Sun "Walkin' on the Sun")" which peaked at number 1 on the US Adult Top 40 and Alternative Songs charts and at number 3 in Canada.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-:0-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-7) The singles "The Fonz" and a cover of "[Why Can't We Be Friends](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Why_Can't_We_Be_Friends_(song) "Why Can't We Be Friends (song)")" from the 1998 Kevin Bacon film _Wild Things_ were also subsequently released. The album has since gone double platinum. During this time the band officially started touring regularly even opening for U2 on their PopMart Tour and got their first television appearance as the musical guest on episode 157 of _Oddville, MTV._[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-8)
texts.4:
### 1998–2004: rise to fame, _Astro Lounge_, _Smash Mouth_, and _Get the Picture?_
[edit | edit source]
The band's second album, _Astro Lounge_, was released in 1999 and marked a change in direction, as it had less of the previous ska influence and more of a pop sound. It led to more publicity for the band, and ended up being one of the most critically acclaimed albums from the group. It peaked at number 6 on the US Billboard 200, the highest the band has ever charted in the states, and reached the top 20 in both Canada and New Zealand.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-9) Supported by the hit single "All Star" (which was featured in several film soundtracks, most notably in _Shrek_ (2001), although the official music video references _Mystery Men_) the song reached number 4 on both the Billboard hot 100 and Australia it then charted even higher in Canada peaking at number 2.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-:0-6)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-10) "Then the Morning Comes" was also a hit for the band and peaked a number 11 on the Billboard hot 100.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-:0-6)_Astro Lounge_ has since been certified as triple platinum.

### Hey Now: a story of alt-rock, soundtracks and fleeting fame
Article and interview Pete Crigler
(December 2023)
Smash Mouth were one of the more popular alt-rock groups of the late '90's, scoring hits with "Walkin' on the Sun" and the ubiquitous "All Star." By the early 2000's, they had pivoted into a more commercial pop direction and after 2001, they dropped off the charts in a supremely quick fashion. Their music always lingered and so did the band, down to two original members, playing state fairs, food and wine festivals and donating songs to Dr. Seuss movies and Hot Wheels video games. In 2021, singer Steve Harwell left the band after a disastrous show, citing mental health and physical maladies including heart issues. In September of 2023, he passed away at the age of 56 because of liver failure. I decided to write about the band's legacy and some of the ways they still resonate even with a lot of crap material in their catalogue.  
The band formed in the mid-'90s after Harwell failed at a rap career, starting a group called F.O.S. and signing a deal with Scotti Bros, home of Weird Al Yankovic. After one failed single, Harwell decided to change tactic. He teamed up with his friend, amateur drummer Kevin Coleman and began devising a new project. By 1995, they had teamed up with guitarist/songwriter Greg Camp and bassist Paul DeLisle and started Smash Mouth. In 1996, the band signed with Interscope and went into the studio with producer Eric Valentine, who was simultaneously working on the debut album by Third Eye Blind. In the summer of 1997, Smash Mouth released _Fush Yu Mang_, a garbled statement made by Al Pacino in _Scarface_. The album's first single was about to change the band's lives forever.

### Hey Now: a story of alt-rock, soundtracks and fleeting fame
That song, a perfect piece of alt-pop written by Greg Camp, "Walkin' on the Sun" was damn near perfect for the summer of 1997 and went to number one on the alternative charts and was all over MTV. It's a song that I still cherish today and think is one of the best alt rock songs of the late '90's. Hooky, very poppy and retro as all hell, the song takes you back to a moment in time and never lets up. One of those songs that to me just feels timeless and sounds good no matter when you're listening to it.
The album is a fun little blast of alt rock with touches of sixties pop and ska amongst others. Good tracks like "Flo," "Disconnect the Dots" and "Let's Rock" are just fun alt rock without too much thought. The album's other main single was a cover of War's "Why Can't We Be Friends" which was featured in _BASEketball_ but hasn't really held up as well. The album eventually went double platinum and the band spent the next year and a half touring and contributing to soundtracks. The most notable was a cover of ? and the Mysterians' "Can't Get Enough of You (Baby)" from the _Can't Hardly Wait_ soundtrack which became the band's next big hit. My personal favorite is a Camp sung track entitled "Sorry About Your Penis," a humorous track found on the soundtrack of the Trey Parker movie _Orgazmo_. Definitely a track worth tracking down for its sheer lunacy and catchiness.

### Hey Now: a story of alt-rock, soundtracks and fleeting fame
Then the band went back to work on their sophomore record. At first in the early part of 1999, Interscope told them they didn't have a single. This led Camp to come up with "Then the Morning Comes." By spring, the album was ready and the label decided to go with "All Star," having decided after all that the album had enough singles. The album, entitled, _Astro Lounge_ was launched in summer of '99 with "All Star." The video was tied to the Ben Stiller superhero comedy _Mystery Men_ and it was quickly all over MTV. The song went to number two on the modern rock chart and crossed over big time to the Billboard Hot 100 where it peaked at number four. The song was one of the most ubiquitous of the year and is still thought of fondly by those of us coming of age around that time.
Drummer Kevin Coleman left during this time and was at first replaced by Tripping Daisy/Brave Combo drummer Mitch Marine before being permanently replaced in 2000 by Cracker/Spent Poets drummer Michael Urbano. "Then the Morning Comes" was released as the second single in late '99 and peaked at number 11 on the hot 100. Around this time, the band began shifting their sound to a more pop oriented flavor, losing a lot of the alternative and ska elements that had helped them initially. The album's third single, a ballad called "Waste," was released in spring of 2000. I had loved the song when it came out but looking back, I must not have remembered it too well for it wasn't as interesting, a little too poppy for my taste. "Then the Morning Comes" has become one of my favorite songs by the band because of the infectiousness and AM-pop leanings of the track. Just a song that deserves to be remembered more.

### Hey Now: a story of alt-rock, soundtracks and fleeting fame
During this time, the band's soundtrack appearances began shifting from the alternative like "Half-Baked" to the more commercial. Though they did contribute a cover of Let's Active's "Every Word Means No" to a _Friends_ comp and a great version of Steely Dan's "Do It Again" to the Jim Carrey comedy _Me, Myself & Irene_, they also appeared with the album track "Come on Come On" for the Nickelodeon kids flick _Snow Day_ and "All Star" was heard in the "Digimon" animated movie, one of many times that song would be used in film. Let's not forget "Better Do It Right" for the Jim Carrey _How the Grinch Stole Christmas_ movie. After touring wrapped sometime in 2000, the band took a break before beginning the next album.
In the spring of 2001, DreamWorks Animation announced their big new film, _Shrek_, which was based on the books by William Steig. The filmmakers needed a song to help introduce the character. The story goes they'd been using "All Star" as a temp track to be replaced by something else but they couldn't find anything else that worked so the song became the lead-in for the whole movie. In addition, the band agreed to record a cover of the Monkees' chestnut "I'm a Believer" for the end credits.
As everyone knows, the film became a blockbuster, one of the biggest hits of the year and one of the most well-regarded animated movies of the early 2000's. "I'm a Believer" became a hit all over again and peaked at number 25 on the hot 100. The movie sealed the reputation of "All Star" as pop culture canon for years to come and even though I couldn't tolerate "I'm a Believer," I couldn't help but think about how amazing it was that the band still had a career as rock groups like them were starting to become a thing of the past. It's here where the story gets a little darker and perhaps foreshadows the end.

**Smash Mouth** is an American rock band from San Jose, California.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-3) The band was formed in 1994[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-4) and was originally composed of Steve Harwell (lead vocals), Kevin Coleman (drums), Greg Camp (guitar), and Paul De Lisle (bass). Harwell's departure in 2021 left De Lisle as the sole remaining original member. They are known for their songs "[Walkin' on the Sun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walkin'_on_the_Sun "Walkin' on the Sun")" (1997), "All Star" (1999),[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-5) and "Then the Morning Comes" (1999), as well as [a cover](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I'm_a_Believer_(Smash_Mouth_song) "I'm a Believer (Smash Mouth song)") of The Monkees' "[I'm a Believer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I'm_a_Believer "I'm a Believer")" (2001).

The band adopted retro styles covering several decades of popular music. They have also performed numerous covers of popular songs, including War's "[Why Can't We Be Friends?](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Why_Can't_We_Be_Friends%3F_(song) "Why Can't We Be Friends? (song)")", Rick Astley's "Never Gonna Give You Up", Simple Minds' "[Don't You (Forget About Me)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don't_You_(Forget_About_Me) "Don't You (Forget About Me)")", ? & the Mysterians' "[Can't Get Enough of You Baby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Can't_Get_Enough_of_You_Baby "Can't Get Enough of You Baby")", the Beatles' "Getting Better", Queen's "Under Pressure", House of Pain's "Jump Around", and "[I Wan'na Be Like You](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Wan'na_Be_Like_You "I Wan'na Be Like You")" from _The Jungle Book_. They also composed two songs for the South Korean animated film _Pororo, The Racing Adventure_: "Beside Myself" and "Everything Just Crazy".
The group's debut album _Fush Yu Mang_ has been certified platinum twice by the RIAA and their second album _Astro Lounge_ has since been certified platinum thrice. Their song "All Star" was nominated for a Grammy Award for Best Pop Performance by a Duo or Group with Vocals in 2001.
Smash Mouth's roots trace back to 1990 when Steve Harwell and Kevin Coleman met. Smash Mouth was then formed in 1994 by Harwell, who had formerly played in a rap group called F.O.S. (Freedom of Speech). Coleman, who was Harwell's manager, knew guitarist Greg Camp and bassist Paul De Lisle, who had both played in a local punk band, and introduced the three musicians to each other. They began rehearsing together along with Coleman, who played drums. They soon developed into a band, and named themselves Smashmouth, an American football term. During their early years, the band played largely rock music.

The band's first publicity came when a demo of the song "Nervous in the Alley" was played by a San Jose radio station, KOME. Soon after, Interscope Records signed the band, and the group's debut album, _Fush Yu Mang_, was released in 1997, featuring another member: the keyboardist Michael Klooster. Also, upon signing to Interscope Records, the band changed their name from Smashmouth to Smash Mouth. The album saw commercial success peaking at number 19 on the US Billboard 200 and number 23 in Canada.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-:0-6) It was led by the band's first major single "[Walkin' on the Sun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walkin'_on_the_Sun "Walkin' on the Sun")" which peaked at number 1 on the US Adult Top 40 and Alternative Songs charts and at number 3 in Canada.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-:0-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-7) The singles "The Fonz" and a cover of "[Why Can't We Be Friends](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Why_Can't_We_Be_Friends_(song) "Why Can't We Be Friends (song)")" from the 1998 Kevin Bacon film _Wild Things_ were also subsequently released. The album has since gone double platinum. During this time the band officially started touring regularly even opening for U2 on their PopMart Tour and got their first television appearance as the musical guest on episode 157 of _Oddville, MTV._[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-8)

### 1998–2004: rise to fame, _Astro Lounge_, _Smash Mouth_, and _Get the Picture?_
[edit | edit source]
The band's second album, _Astro Lounge_, was released in 1999 and marked a change in direction, as it had less of the previous ska influence and more of a pop sound. It led to more publicity for the band, and ended up being one of the most critically acclaimed albums from the group. It peaked at number 6 on the US Billboard 200, the highest the band has ever charted in the states, and reached the top 20 in both Canada and New Zealand.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-9) Supported by the hit single "All Star" (which was featured in several film soundtracks, most notably in _Shrek_ (2001), although the official music video references _Mystery Men_) the song reached number 4 on both the Billboard hot 100 and Australia it then charted even higher in Canada peaking at number 2.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-:0-6)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-10) "Then the Morning Comes" was also a hit for the band and peaked a number 11 on the Billboard hot 100.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-:0-6)_Astro Lounge_ has since been certified as triple platinum.
